paper_metadata.title: A Quantum Algorithm for Pricing Asian Options on Valuation Trees

summary: The paper presents a gate-based quantum algorithm for pricing discrete floating-strike Asian options on valuation trees using amplitude encoding, amplitude arithmetic, and a gearbox-style positive-part circuit. It reports simulator-based results for a Rendleman-Bartter binomial model with n = 2 to 6 time steps, gearbox approximation levels D = 1 and 2, Fourier terms n_f = 4, 5, 8, 16, and circuit widths ranging from 13 to 23 qubits with cX counts from 67 to 1229 depending on the parameter setting.

experiments.description: Quantum simulation of a gate-based circuit for pricing discrete floating-strike Asian options on valuation trees, evaluated for a binomial Rendleman-Bartter model with varying time steps and positive-part approximation settings.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude-based valuation-tree Asian option pricing with amplitude arithmetic and gearbox-style positive-part approximation; compatible with amplitude estimation

hyperparameters.state_register_encoding: uniform superposition over valuation-tree paths via Hadamard gates
hyperparameters.positive_part_approximation: gearbox circuit GbD with Fourier-series approximation

algorithm.parameter_initialization: State register initialized either in computational basis states for single-path evaluation or uniform superposition via Hadamard gates for full pricing runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per time step for the binomial valuation tree; each path is represented by an n-qubit computational basis state, with path probabilities loaded into amplitudes. Payoff and indicator are encoded into additional ancilla qubits via controlled rotations and amplitude arithmetic.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Positive part implemented approximately by gearbox circuit; amplitude subtraction and multi-controlled X used to combine terms; no explicit penalty formulation
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: At least ceil(log2(n)) ancillas for G plus additional ancillas for gearbox circuit and readout qubits; exact total varies by subcircuit and is not fully enumerated

problem_instance.description: Discrete floating-strike Asian option on a binomial Rendleman-Bartter valuation tree

dataset_specification.description: S(0)=1, zero interest r=0, sigma=0.2, up/down factors u and d as given in Eq. (29), equal up/down probabilities 1/2

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Classical precomputation of underlying values on the valuation tree; scaling by M=max_{t_i,k} S_k(t_i) to map values into [0,1]
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single-path circuit evaluations for representative paths; full pricing via 100 histogram data points, each from 10^6 circuit shots; path-evaluation figure uses 10^7 shots

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical computation of valuation-tree node values and scaling constants; construction of path probabilities and payoff terms
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rescaling measured probabilities to option price; histogram averaging over repeated circuit runs

speedup_claims.conditions: if the circuit is combined with quantum amplitude estimation and sufficiently large fault-tolerant quantum hardware is available
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the algorithm is compatible with amplitude estimation and could achieve quadratic speed-up, but the reported experiments were run on a simulator without amplitude estimation due to circuit depth restrictions.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/N_s) convergence for amplitude estimation; circuit resources dominated by uniformly controlled rotations with O(2^n) cX-gate applications for state preparation

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Amplitude estimation would require a fault-tolerant setting and sufficiently deep circuits; the paper only reports simulator runs with 1e6-1e8 shots and no end-to-end runtime comparison against classical Monte Carlo.
limiting_factors: No experimental classical-vs-quantum advantage benchmark is reported
Circuit depth is not fully quantified and the paper notes current hardware is too limited
State preparation is exponential in general for arbitrary distributions
Quadratic AE speedup is only theoretical in this work

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_other because the paper states evaluations were performed with a simulator for a quantum computer and specifically mentions the Qiskit simulator; no real QPU device is named.
num_qubits and gate counts are taken from Table 1 for the three parameter combinations and varying n; the paper reports circuit width rather than a single fixed qubit count.
circuit_depth is not explicitly reported; set to null.
The authors explicitly describe a theoretical quadratic speedup via amplitude estimation, but they do not demonstrate practical advantage over classical methods.
Results are from a Qiskit simulator, with no real hardware benchmark and no classical runtime comparison.
